 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22

 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Thunder and Cason Wallace agreed to a five-year, $139 million extension. 
 Wallace and the Thunder had until Monday at 6 PM Eastern to agree to a rookie-scale extension, and they got it done on Sunday night. With the Thunder trading Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe, and Aaron Wiggins during the offseason, Wallace moves into a full-time starting role. He was close to a top-100 player in category leagues last season, and that may represent Wallace’s floor in 2026-27. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Cason Wallace accounted for seven points (2-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 Like Oklahoma City’s other projected starters, Wallace sat out the team’s preseason opener on Tuesday. He logged 18 minutes on Wednesday, dishing out six assists without committing a turnover. Wallace didn’t have a great night shooting the ball, but he did a little bit of everything else. He was the fifth starter on most nights last season when Oklahoma City was down a man, and it appears Wallace will be a full-time starter following the trade of Luguentz Dort. That makes him a more appealing option within the first 100 picks in standard drafts. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Thunder general manager Sam Presti names Cason Wallace, Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain as players that will play more minutes this season. 
 Not only will all three take on larger roles with Luguentz Dort now in Atlanta, but Presti is expecting genuine jumps in their production. All 3 players had strong stretches for OKC last season, and they’ll be relied on once again to help the Thunder get back on track after losing in the Western Conference Finals last season. Wallace seems like the most likely choice to start, but Mitchell and McCain will play big minutes off the bench. 
 Luguentz Dort 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Luguentz Dort said on Sunday that his “main goal” is to remain with the Thunder. 
 Oklahoma City’s season came to an end on Saturday, as they dropped Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals to the Spurs. And with that, the front office has decisions to make regarding the futures of Dort, Isaiah Hartenstein and Kenrich Williams. Each has a team option for next season, with Dort’s being worth a little over $17.7 million. The defensive stalwart hopes to remain with the lone team that he’s played for since entering the NBA in 2019. “The conversation hasn’t happened yet,” Dort said when asked about his team option. “I have a lot of trust in this organization, in Sam (Presti). Really grateful for all the stuff he did for me to this point. I want to stay here. This organization, this city, shaped me as a player. My main goal is to stay here.” Dort has not been a consistently impactful option for fantasy managers in recent seasons. Still, his future in Oklahoma City could affect the ceilings of Ajay Mitchell, Cason Wallace and Jared McCain. If the Thunder were to move on from Dort, there would be an opening in the starting lineup to fill. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Cason Wallace accounted for 17 points (6-of-10 FGs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Saturday’s Game 7 loss to the Spurs. 
 Making his second start of the Western Conference Finals, Wallace stepped up with his best performance of the 2026 NBA Playoffs. The Thunder guard shot 5-of-9 from beyond the arc and recorded a complete stat line. On a night when three other starters failed to score in double figures, Wallace was one of Oklahoma City’s most capable options in Game 7. Due to the team’s depth, his fantasy ceiling has been somewhat limited, but Wallace has been a solid option in category leagues. He’ll be extension eligible this summer, and a larger role could be in the cards for 2026-27, especially considering Luguentz Dort’s struggles. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Cason Wallace, Luguentz Dort, Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Saturday’s Game 7 against the Spurs. 
 After calling on Jared McCain to serve as the fifth starter in Games 5 and 6, the Thunder turn to Wallace to fill the void left by Jalen Williams (hamstring). The third-year guard started Game 4, logging 21 minutes and finishing with five points, four rebounds, one assist, two steals and one three-pointer. Wallace will look to offer greater production on Saturday, with the winner headed to the NBA Finals. Despite moving to the bench, McCain will still figure prominently in the Thunder rotation. 
 Jalen Williams 
 OKC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #8 
 Jalen Williams (hamstring) will not play against the Spurs on Tuesday. 
 Williams’ third straight absence puts the Thunder in a tougher spot, as they’ll also be without Ajay Mitchell (calf). Williams hasn’t played since Game 2 of the series, logging just seven first-quarter minutes before being ruled out the rest of the way. His presence will be missed, placing extra importance on players such as Jared McCain, Cason Wallace, and Isaiah Joe to fill the void in production for a Thunder team looking to protect homecourt and take a 3-2 series lead. 
 Jared McCain 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Jared McCain, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Chet Holmgren, Isaiah Hartenstein and Luguentz Dort will start against the Spurs on Tuesday. 
 McCain will start for the first time during this Western Conference Finals matchup, as the Thunder look to bounce back from a blowout loss in Game 4. He will replace Cason Wallace in the opening unit, who had served as a replacement starter for the still-injured Jalen Williams (hamstring). McCain’s scoring production has fluctuated throughout the series, but he offers high-scoring potential. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell (calf) is out for Game 5 against the Spurs on Tuesday. 
 Mitchell moved into the starting lineup for Game 3 of the series with Jalen Williams (hamstring) sidelined. He suffered a right calf strain and was ruled out for Game 4 and Game 5. Cason Wallace started Game 4 and might have to start Game 5 too with Williams listed as questionable. 
 Cason Wallace 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Cason Wallace accounted for five points (2-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, one assist, two steals and one three-pointer in Sunday’s Game 4 loss to the Spurs. 
 With Jalen Williams (hamstring) and Ajay Mitchell (calf) unavailable, the Thunder turned to Wallace to fill the resulting void in the starting lineup. He struggled with his shot in Game 4, but the third-year guard wasn’t the only one who failed to show up. Jared McCain (four points, two rebounds) shot 1-of-10 from the field and Alex Caruso (two rebounds, one assist and two blocks) missed his lone shot attempt. Regardless of what happens with J-Dub and Mitchell for Tuesday’s Game 5, the Thunder need more from Wallace, McCain and Caruso if they’re to defend home court.

 Jalen Brunson produced 28 points (12-of-28 FGs, 3-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, two steals, one block and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Magic.
 Brunson led all scorers with 28 points, but the Magic made him work for every shot that he took. The Knicks’ point guard needed 28 field-goal attempts to reach that total, and he made 1-of-7 from beyond the arc. As a team, New York shot 9-of-38 from three while Orlando was 18-of-42. Essentially, that was the ballgame. Brunson has been inefficient as a scorer so far, and things won’t get any easier for him when the Pistons visit MSG on Tuesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 OG Anunoby amassed 22 points (6-of-11 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), three rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Magic.
 Anunoby has scored 20 or more points in consecutive games and shot a respectable percentage against the Magic on Sunday. His final stat line didn’t include any defensive stats, but that is not usually a concern for OG over an entire season. More concerning, the Knicks still haven’t won a game, and Sunday’s defeat dropped the reigning champs to 0-3. New York plays three games in Week 2, starting Tuesday against the Pistons.

 Desmond Bane accounted for 22 points (6-of-13 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, two blocks and four three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Knicks.
 In Orlando’s first two games, Bane shot 26.9 percent from the field and 21.1 percent from beyond the arc. To say he needed a night like Sunday is an understatement. Bane shot 4-of-9 from deep, and his 22 points were one less than his total in losses to the Hawks and Timberwolves. In addition to Paolo Banchero, the Magic could be without Jalen Suggs for an extended period after he injured his right knee in the fourth quarter. As a result, they’ll need more scoring from Bane.

 Tristan da Silva recorded 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), two rebounds, two assists, one block and five three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Knicks.
 While the Magic started Jase Richardson (3 points, 1 three-pointer in 10 minutes) for the injured Paolo Banchero on Sunday, this was a prime spot for da Silva to provide greater fantasy value. That’s exactly what he did: he shot 5-of-9 from three and scored 19 of Orlando’s 47 bench points. The Magic also lost Jalen Suggs (knee) on Sunday, and a potential extended absence is another reason to add da Silva if he’s available. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Anthony Black finished Sunday’s win over the Knicks with 18 points (6-of-11 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers.
 After missing the entire preseason and Orlando’s first two games with a sprained ankle, Black made his first appearance on Sunday. He was excellent, especially in the first quarter, scoring 12 points off the bench. With Paolo Banchero (ankle) likely out for 4-6 weeks and Jalen Suggs (knee) going down during the fourth quarter, Black’s return came at a great time for Orlando. Even though the Magic don’t play their next game until Wednesday, fantasy managers should add Black if he’s sitting on the waiver wire.

 RJ Barrett finished Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 20 points (9-of-21 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, two assists and three steals.
 Barrett helped keep the Raptors within striking distance of the Timberwolves in the first half, scoring 14 points. Unfortunately for him, he went cold in the third quarter, along with the rest of the Raptors, shooting 1-of-5 from the field. Toronto was outscored 35-15 as Kawhi Leonard’s absence and Scottie Barnes’ 0-of-12 shooting caught up to them. Barrett and the Raptors will look to bounce back on Wednesday against the Magic. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Immanuel Quickley amassed 19 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-3 Fts), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Quickley had a productive night, but it didn’t matter much when two other Raptors starters (Scottie Barnes and Jakob Poeltl) went scoreless, shooting 0-of-14 from the field combined. IQ’s current fantasy value doesn’t align with his preseason ADP, but he’s a relatively safe bet for at least top-100 value. The Raptors play three games in Week 2, starting with the Magic on Wednesday.

 Ja’Kobe Walter accounted for 22 points (7-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Due to Kawhi Leonard’s swollen left knee, Walter was plugged into the Raptors’ starting lineup on Sunday. He was one of the few who had productive nights, shooting over 50 percent from the field and leading the Raptors in scoring. Walter’s fantasy value will hinge on who else the Raptors have available each night, most notably Leonard. But Sunday’s performance showed that he’s a worthwhile streamer when starting.

 Terrence Shannon Jr. accounted for 15 points (5-of-6 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
 The Timberwolves’ bench accounted for 41 of the team’s 117 points, led by Shannon with 15. He’s scored in double figures in all three of Minnesota’s games, but he still has work to do to become a reliable option in category leagues. Ayo Dosunmu (9/3/3 with one three-pointer) remains the better option for fantasy managers looking for value on the Timberwolves bench, even after a quiet night against the Raptors.

 Kuminga’s gotten off to a good start in Minnesota, providing consistent supplementary scoring as a starter for the Timberwolves. He won’t get many shots in a lineup headlined by Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, and Jaden McDaniels, but he’ll have enough opportunities to provide reliable value. Rostered in 56 percent of Yahoo leagues, JK has been a top-100 player in category leagues so far.
